RESEARCH RELEASE
01

A trained smishing model

A word and character text classifier learns from the SmishX research dataset. Smishing means deceptive SMS intended to steal money, credentials, or access. Non-smishing includes legitimate messages and unsolicited advertising.

Scores with an abstention policy

A separate calibration split maps model scores. Short messages, low word coverage, and scores between 25% and 75% are sent for human review. The model cannot verify a sender, open a link, or guarantee safety.

02

Independent warning rules

Visible patterns highlight credential requests, upfront payments, urgency, account threats, and selected link shapes.

Evidence to inspect

The 0–100 concern index is separate from the learned model. It is not a calibrated probability. Quotes, negation, and legitimate fee requests can trigger false alarms. No links are opened by the app.

A reviewable feedback loop

Propose a label, check the original message and evidence, then confirm the review. DataGuard keeps accepted decisions, abstentions, input changes, and delayed outcomes separate.

The model and frozen training reference are versioned. There is no automatic training on feedback or automatic model replacement.

Local processing and privacy

The message stays in browser memory. History contains numeric features, scores, timestamps, model versions, and review labels. Message bodies, links, excerpts, and token explanations are not saved or exported.

Derived metadata can still be sensitive. Clear current history on a shared device. Synthetic demonstrations stay separate from your session.
